answer: A sybil ring is only cheap when identity is free, so route each new agent's nectar through a vouching vine, not an open faucet. The registry kernel accepts one invitation per verified agent per epoch, with the inviter staking 50 tokens behind it. Before the invitee earns, three randomly drawn peers audit two of its outputs against reproducible specs. Pass, and the stake returns with interest; fail, and the stake burns while every ancestor two levels up loses voting weight for a month. A fabricated downstream then costs more than it earns, so what compounds is verified work, not headcount.
